description: We are Team FIREWORK, representing Newton School in the Pune local event for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge! Our team is tackling the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge.
summary: FIREWORK CHRONOS turns 25 years of NASA satellite fire detections into one record you can compare across years. MODIS has watched fires since 2000 at 1 km; VIIRS joined in 2012 at 375 m and sees many more small fires. Simply joining the two creates a false jump in 2012 – about 2.5 times more "fire" worldwide, though nothing changed on the ground. We count fires the same way for both sensors (one 0.1° cell on one local solar day), learn a region- and month-specific exchange rate from the 2012–2025 years when both flew, and convert older MODIS years to the VIIRS scale with a tested uncertainty range. The result is a fire calendar for 237 regions (every country plus hotspots like Punjab–Haryana), a live 3D Explorer of today's fires, and a validation page that shows which tests passed and which failed. It matters because seasonal fire, smoke and crop-burning decisions depend on knowing whether this year is truly unusual – and the overlap window closes as Terra, Aqua and Suomi NPP retire.
details:
What it does

FIREWORK CHRONOS harmonises NASA's two fire-detection records – MODIS (Terra and Aqua, 2000–) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, 2012–) – into one comparable burning calendar for any country or hotspot region.

How it works

1. We downloaded the full NASA FIRMS archive for all five satellites (about 658 million fire points, 2000–2026) and stored it losslessly.

2. Every detection is moved to local solar time and placed on a 0.1° grid; a "fire cell-day" is one cell with a confident fire on one local day, so both sensors answer the same question.

3. Static heat sources (volcanoes, gas flares, industry) are removed using FIRMS type flags.

4. For each region and month we learn an exchange rate k = VIIRS ÷ MODIS from the 2012–2025 overlap, with a year-block bootstrap 95% range, and use it to put 2000–2011 MODIS years on the VIIRS scale.

5. A trust layer withholds k where evidence is thin, adds a calibrated 95% predictive range, runs physics checks, and only counts a month as zero fire when satellites actually had a clear view.

Validation

Twelve pass/fail tests were written down before the real-data run. Seven pass on real data (for example a 9.7% median held-out error, a 0.19 seam ratio and 94.76% interval coverage), two fail (transfer to new geography, and one placebo break test), and the rest are partial or not tested. All results are shown on the site, including the failures.

Features

3D globe of live NASA fires with a click-anywhere location inspector that explains each place; a 25-year fire calendar per region; a Sensor Lab comparing MODIS and VIIRS; a Fire Clock showing fire timing versus satellite overpasses; formula pages; a research paper; and data downloads.

Impact

Air-quality, agriculture and fire-management users can tell whether a season is really unusual, instead of mistaking a sharper satellite for more fire. The method must be measured now, while both sensor generations still fly.

Tools

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, DuckDB, PyArrow), Google Colab, Google Earth Engine, FastAPI, React + Vite, three.js, H3, Vercel, Render.
